title: ABG case 01
حالة غازات دم 01
vignette: A patient with a severe asthma exacerbation, working hard to breathe, now tiring.

question.prompt: Based on this gas panel, what is the acid-base interpretation?
options: Respiratory acidosis with an acute-compatible bicarbonate response
question.explanation: Elevated PaCO2 explains the acidemia. Bicarbonate is modestly increased, compatible with an acute respiratory disturbance in this vignette; one gas cannot prove duration. Increasing fatigue in severe asthma requires urgent assessment.

oxygenationNote: PaO2 65 mmHg on FiO2 0.4 gives a P/F ratio of 162.5.
evidenceSources: American Thoracic Society — Interpretation of ABGs: https://site.thoracic.org/assemblies/cc/clinical-education/interpretation-of-abgs

title: ABG case 02
حالة غازات دم 02
vignette: A patient with new-onset diabetic ketoacidosis.

question.prompt: Based on this gas panel, what is the acid-base interpretation?
options: Metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation within the expected range
question.explanation: The low bicarbonate is consistent with metabolic acidosis. Winter's estimate for PaCO2 is 21.5 mmHg, with an approximate range of 19.5–23.5. The measured 22 falls within that range despite ongoing acidemia. The clinical team must assess the anion gap and cause.

evidenceSources: American Thoracic Society — Interpretation of ABGs: https://site.thoracic.org/assemblies/cc/clinical-education/interpretation-of-abgs

title: ABG case 03
حالة غازات دم 03
vignette: An anxious patient hyperventilating after a panic episode.

question.prompt: Based on this gas panel, what is the acid-base interpretation?
options: Respiratory alkalosis with an acute-compatible bicarbonate response
question.explanation: Low PaCO2 explains alkalemia. Bicarbonate is modestly reduced, consistent with an early buffering response. The history may support acute hyperventilation, but other causes of tachypnoea must be assessed before attributing it to anxiety.

evidenceSources: American Thoracic Society — Interpretation of ABGs: https://site.thoracic.org/assemblies/cc/clinical-education/interpretation-of-abgs

title: ABG case 04
حالة غازات دم 04
vignette: A patient with prolonged vomiting and nasogastric suction losses.

question.prompt: Based on this gas panel, what is the acid-base interpretation?
options: Metabolic alkalosis with respiratory compensation within the expected range
question.explanation: The raised bicarbonate explains alkalemia. PaCO2 of 46 is within the approximate expected range of 46–47.5 for bicarbonate 34. Compensation can be appropriate even while pH remains outside the reference interval.

title: ABG case 05
حالة غازات دم 05
vignette: A patient with longstanding COPD, at their usual baseline, feeling well.

question.prompt: Based on this gas panel, what is the acid-base interpretation?
options: Respiratory acidosis with no bicarbonate rise
Respiratory acidosis with elevated bicarbonate compatible with chronic compensation
question.explanation: PaCO2 is elevated and pH is low. The bicarbonate rise is compatible with longer-standing adaptation in the context of known COPD. A single gas cannot establish chronicity or exclude a superimposed disorder; compare prior results and the patient's status.

oxygenationNote: PaO2 58 mmHg on FiO2 0.28 gives a P/F ratio of approximately 207.1; assess oxygenation and the clinical context.
evidenceSources: American Thoracic Society — Interpretation of ABGs: https://site.thoracic.org/assemblies/cc/clinical-education/interpretation-of-abgs

title: ABG case 06
حالة غازات دم 06
vignette: A patient in septic shock with lactic acidosis, now also showing early respiratory fatigue.

question.prompt: Based on this gas panel, what is the acid-base interpretation?
options: Isolated metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
question.explanation: Low bicarbonate and elevated PaCO2 both contribute to severe acidemia. Expected PaCO2 for bicarbonate 12 is about 26 ± 2 mmHg, far below the measured 48. This suggests concurrent respiratory acidosis in addition to metabolic acidosis and warrants urgent clinical assessment.

oxygenationNote: PaO2 70 mmHg on FiO2 0.5 gives a P/F ratio of 140.
evidenceSources: American Thoracic Society — Interpretation of ABGs: https://site.thoracic.org/assemblies/cc/clinical-education/interpretation-of-abgs

title: ABG case 07

vignette: A ventilated patient with ARDS on a high FiO2.

question.prompt: Based on this gas panel, what is the acid-base interpretation?
options: No apparent acid-base disturbance in the displayed values
question.explanation: The displayed acid-base values fall within the teaching reference intervals; this does not exclude hidden metabolic disorders. PaO2 of 68 on FiO2 0.8 is concerning, with a P/F ratio of 85. Oxygenation and ventilatory support require separate assessment; P/F alone is not an ARDS diagnosis.

title: ABG case 08
حالة غازات دم 08
vignette: A patient with suspected sepsis, tachypnoea and a low bicarbonate result, despite a pH within the usual reference interval.

question.prompt: What is the safest interpretation of this gas panel?
options: Possible mixed metabolic acidosis and respiratory alkalosis
Full compensation proven by normal pH
question.explanation: With bicarbonate 12, Winter's expected PaCO2 is about 26 ± 2 mmHg. The measured 20 is below that estimate, suggesting a concurrent respiratory alkalosis if metabolic acidosis is present. A normal pH can hide opposing processes. Assess the clinical context, electrolytes, anion gap and trends rather than assuming normality.

evidenceSources: American Thoracic Society — Interpretation of ABGs: https://site.thoracic.org/assemblies/cc/clinical-education/interpretation-of-abgs
